children.text: The Design of a Nuclear Reactor

A cylindrical reactor of radius \(R\) and height \(H\) contains natural \(\mathrm{UO_2}\) fuel pins, grouped in vertical fuel channels on a square lattice. Fission neutrons lose energy by colliding with moderator material, then cause further fission. Natural uranium contains 0.720 percent \({}^{235}\mathrm U\). For \(\mathrm{UO_2}\), use molar mass \(M_w=0.270\,\mathrm{kg/mol}\), density \(\rho=1.060\times10^4\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), melting point \(T_m=3138\,\mathrm K\), and thermal conductivity \(\lambda=3.280\,\mathrm{W/(m\,K)}\). Use \(N_A=6.022\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\).

Find the number of uranium-235 atoms per unit fuel volume.

Uniform neutron flux is \(\phi=2.000\times10^{18}\,\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}\), fission cross-section \(\sigma_f=5.400\times10^{-26}\,\mathrm{m^2}\). If 80 percent of fission energy becomes heat, find \(Q\). Use \(1\,\mathrm{MeV}=1.602\times10^{-13}\,\mathrm J\).
A pin of radius \(a\) has \(T_c-T_s=F(Q,a,\lambda)/4\). Determine \(F\) by dimensional analysis.
The desired coolant temperature is \(T_s=577.0\,\mathrm K\). Estimate the largest radius avoiding melting at the centre.

children.text: A neutron of mass 1 u and incoming laboratory velocity \(\mathbf v_b\) collides elastically with a stationary moderator atom of mass \(A\,\mathrm u\). Its outgoing laboratory velocity is \(\mathbf v_a\), and CM velocity is \(\mathbf v_m\). Draw the CM collision and label initial neutron, final neutron and initial moderator velocities, and neutron scattering angle \(\theta\).
Find neutron and moderator speeds \(v,V\) after collision in the CM frame.
Derive \(G(\alpha,\theta)=E_a/E_b\), where \(\alpha=[(A-1)/(A+1)]^2\) and energies refer to the laboratory frame.
Apply this model to a \(\mathrm{D_2O}\) molecule of mass 20 u. Find the maximum fractional neutron energy loss.

Leakage rate is \(k_1[(2.405/R)^2+(\pi/H)^2]\psi\), and excess production rate is \(k_2\psi\), with \(k_1=1.021\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm m\), \(k_2=8.787\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^{-1}}\). Minimize leakage for fixed cylindrical volume, then find steady-state dimensions.
The square lattice spacing is 0.286 m, and each channel has effective solid fuel radius \(r_f=3.617\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm m\). Estimate number of channels and fuel mass.

statement.text:
The Design of a Nuclear Reactor
A cylindrical reactor of radius \(R\) and height \(H\) contains natural \(\mathrm{UO_2}\) fuel pins, grouped in vertical fuel channels on a square lattice. Fission neutrons lose energy by colliding with moderator material, then cause further fission. Natural uranium contains 0.720 percent \({}^{235}\mathrm U\). For \(\mathrm{UO_2}\), use molar mass \(M_w=0.270\,\mathrm{kg/mol}\), density \(\rho=1.060\times10^4\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), melting point \(T_m=3138\,\mathrm K\), and thermal conductivity \(\lambda=3.280\,\mathrm{W/(m\,K)}\). Use \(N_A=6.022\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\).

A1. Fission energy
For \({}^{235}\mathrm U+n\to{}^{94}\mathrm{Zr}+{}^{140}\mathrm{Ce}+2n\), estimate released energy, ignoring charge imbalance. Nuclear masses are 235.044 u, 93.9063 u, 139.905 u and neutron mass 1.00867 u. Use \(1\,\mathrm u=931.502\,\mathrm{MeV}/c^2\).
A2. Fissile number density
Find the number of uranium-235 atoms per unit fuel volume.
A3. Volumetric heating
Uniform neutron flux is \(\phi=2.000\times10^{18}\,\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}\), fission cross-section \(\sigma_f=5.400\times10^{-26}\,\mathrm{m^2}\). If 80 percent of fission energy becomes heat, find \(Q\). Use \(1\,\mathrm{MeV}=1.602\times10^{-13}\,\mathrm J\).
A4. Fuel temperature scale
A pin of radius \(a\) has \(T_c-T_s=F(Q,a,\lambda)/4\). Determine \(F\) by dimensional analysis.
A5. Largest fuel pin radius
The desired coolant temperature is \(T_s=577.0\,\mathrm K\). Estimate the largest radius avoiding melting at the centre.
B1. Centre-of-mass collision drawing

A neutron of mass 1 u and incoming laboratory velocity \(\mathbf v_b\) collides elastically with a stationary moderator atom of mass \(A\,\mathrm u\). Its outgoing laboratory velocity is \(\mathbf v_a\), and CM velocity is \(\mathbf v_m\). Draw the CM collision and label initial neutron, final neutron and initial moderator velocities, and neutron scattering angle \(\theta\).
B2. Post-collision CM speeds
Find neutron and moderator speeds \(v,V\) after collision in the CM frame.
B3. Neutron energy ratio
Derive \(G(\alpha,\theta)=E_a/E_b\), where \(\alpha=[(A-1)/(A+1)]^2\) and energies refer to the laboratory frame.
B4. Maximum moderator energy loss
Apply this model to a \(\mathrm{D_2O}\) molecule of mass 20 u. Find the maximum fractional neutron energy loss.
C1. Efficient reactor dimensions
Leakage rate is \(k_1[(2.405/R)^2+(\pi/H)^2]\psi\), and excess production rate is \(k_2\psi\), with \(k_1=1.021\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm m\), \(k_2=8.787\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^{-1}}\). Minimize leakage for fixed cylindrical volume, then find steady-state dimensions.
C2. Fuel channels and mass
The square lattice spacing is 0.286 m, and each channel has effective solid fuel radius \(r_f=3.617\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm m\). Estimate number of channels and fuel mass.

children.text: The Design of a Nuclear Reactor
\(Q\) has units \(\mathrm{W/m^3}\), while \(\lambda\) has units \(\mathrm{W/(m\,K)}\), so \(F=Qa^2/\lambda\).

Subtract \(\mathbf v_m=\mathbf v_b/(A+1)\) from every laboratory velocity. Initial neutron is \(\mathbf v_b-\mathbf v_m\), final neutron \(\mathbf v_a-\mathbf v_m\), initial moderator \(-\mathbf v_m\). The outgoing CM momenta are equal and opposite. Mark \(\theta\) between incoming and outgoing neutron directions.
CM momentum gives \(v=AV\). Elastic energy conservation leaves the incoming CM speed magnitudes unchanged: \(v=Av_b/(A+1)\), \(V=v_b/(A+1)\).
Add CM translation to the outgoing neutron velocity: \(v_a^2=v^2+v_m^2+2vv_m\cos\theta\). Therefore \[G=\frac{A^2+1+2A\cos\theta}{(A+1)^2}=\frac{1+\alpha+(1-\alpha)\cos\theta}{2}.\]
Backscattering gives the minimum retained fraction \(\alpha\). Hence \(f_{loss}=1-(19/21)^2=80/441=0.1814\).

At fixed \(R^2H\), differentiating leakage gives \(H/R=\sqrt2\pi/2.405\). At the optimum the radial leakage term is twice the axial term. Steady balance yields \[R=2.405\sqrt{\frac{3k_1}{2k_2}}=3.175\,\mathrm m,\qquad H=\pi\sqrt{\frac{3k_1}{k_2}}=5.866\,\mathrm m.\]
Area per channel is \(s^2\), so \(F_n\simeq\pi R^2/s^2=387\). Total fuel mass is \(M=F_n\pi r_f^2H\rho\simeq9.89\times10^4\,\mathrm{kg}\). Boundary rounding is part of the estimate.

solution.text:
The Design of a Nuclear Reactor
A1. Fission energy
The mass defect is \(235.044-93.9063-139.905-1.00867=0.22403\,\mathrm u\). Thus \(E_f=208.7\,\mathrm{MeV}\).
A2. Fissile number density
\(N=0.00720\rho N_A/M_w=1.70\times10^{26}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\).
A3. Volumetric heating
The reaction rate is \(N\sigma_f\phi\). Hence \(Q=0.8E_fN\sigma_f\phi=4.92\times10^8\,\mathrm{W/m^3}\).
A4. Fuel temperature scale
\(Q\) has units \(\mathrm{W/m^3}\), while \(\lambda\) has units \(\mathrm{W/(m\,K)}\), so \(F=Qa^2/\lambda\).
A5. Largest fuel pin radius
Impose \(T_c\le T_m\). Thus \(a_u=\sqrt{4\lambda(T_m-T_s)/Q}=8.27\,\mathrm{mm}\).
B1. Centre-of-mass collision drawing
Subtract \(\mathbf v_m=\mathbf v_b/(A+1)\) from every laboratory velocity. Initial neutron is \(\mathbf v_b-\mathbf v_m\), final neutron \(\mathbf v_a-\mathbf v_m\), initial moderator \(-\mathbf v_m\). The outgoing CM momenta are equal and opposite. Mark \(\theta\) between incoming and outgoing neutron directions.
B2. Post-collision CM speeds
CM momentum gives \(v=AV\). Elastic energy conservation leaves the incoming CM speed magnitudes unchanged: \(v=Av_b/(A+1)\), \(V=v_b/(A+1)\).
B3. Neutron energy ratio
Add CM translation to the outgoing neutron velocity: \(v_a^2=v^2+v_m^2+2vv_m\cos\theta\). Therefore \[G=\frac{A^2+1+2A\cos\theta}{(A+1)^2}=\frac{1+\alpha+(1-\alpha)\cos\theta}{2}.\]
B4. Maximum moderator energy loss
Backscattering gives the minimum retained fraction \(\alpha\). Hence \(f_{loss}=1-(19/21)^2=80/441=0.1814\).
C1. Efficient reactor dimensions
At fixed \(R^2H\), differentiating leakage gives \(H/R=\sqrt2\pi/2.405\). At the optimum the radial leakage term is twice the axial term. Steady balance yields \[R=2.405\sqrt{\frac{3k_1}{2k_2}}=3.175\,\mathrm m,\qquad H=\pi\sqrt{\frac{3k_1}{k_2}}=5.866\,\mathrm m.\]
C2. Fuel channels and mass
Area per channel is \(s^2\), so \(F_n\simeq\pi R^2/s^2=387\). Total fuel mass is \(M=F_n\pi r_f^2H\rho\simeq9.89\times10^4\,\mathrm{kg}\). Boundary rounding is part of the estimate.
